# Streamed container chain

These generated QCOW2 v3 images contain the existing disposable
[`devices/mbr.img.gz`](../devices/README.md) disk: MBR → ext4 →
`папка 空/данные с пробелом.txt`. No real device or user data is used.

The virtual disk is 1 GiB, mostly unallocated or explicit zero clusters.
`stored.qcow2.gz` contains stored clusters; `deflate.qcow2.gz` also contains
independently Deflate-compressed clusters. `zstd.qcow2.gz` is produced by
`qemu-img` with Zstandard compression. The outer gzip only keeps the fixture
small in the repository; tests decompress it before opening QCOW2.
The `extended-*` images are generated by QEMU with extended L2 entries, using
stored, Deflate and Zstandard clusters, and compared with the same raw disk.
The `qcow1-*` fixtures exercise legacy QCOW1 stored and compressed clusters.
QEMU creates them and compares their decoded bytes with the raw source;
QCOW1 has no `qemu-img check` implementation. Its compressed fixture uses
`qemu-io` to write complete compressed clusters.
The shortened-Deflate variant omits the last encoded byte of one cluster;
QEMU still confirms the complete raw disk, exercising its full-output reading rule.
`reference_sets` in the manifest describes dependent images and their local file
names. QEMU generates these backing-chain/external-data fixtures and the expected
raw disk; they contain disposable patterned bytes and no user data.
`snapshot_sets` contains QEMU-created internal snapshots: ordinary v2 tables,
extended L2 with Zstandard, a raw backing dependency, and an MBR/ext4 disk.
QEMU's temporary snapshot loader supplies the expected disk bytes. Since that
loader retains active geometry, shorter snapshots' expected output is bounded
to their saved geometry after confirming its remaining bytes are zero. Only
fixture timestamps are fixed for reproducible regeneration; QEMU checks the
resulting images. Snapshot names include an unsafe path to exercise metadata
display without using that name as an extraction path.
`manifest.json` records the raw source/image sizes, SHA-256 hashes and expected
selected file bytes. The encoder follows the
[QEMU QCOW2 specification](https://www.qemu.org/docs/master/interop/qcow2.html).
It is test data generation, not a product decoder. The Zstandard fixture is
validated by `qemu-img check` and byte comparison with its raw source; no guest
OS is booted.

Regenerate with Python 3, `qemu-img` and `qemu-io` available on PATH:

```sh
python3 scripts/generate-qcow-fixtures.py tests/fixtures/layers
```

Nothing is mounted or attached. The QCOW regression compares the readable disk
prefix with the raw source, checks backward and sparse-tail reads, and rejects
unsupported layouts and damaged Zstandard data through the official handler.
